title: Disagreement at home
paragraphs: The information gathered abroad entered a society already debating foreign relations, political authority, and the preservation of existing institutions. Some officials argued for selective adaptation. Others feared that rapid reform would weaken the social order or expose the state to unwanted external influence. Reducing these debates to enlightened reformers versus backward conservatives obscures the difficult choices people believed they faced.

A reform proposal has consequences for the institutions and people required to carry it out. Importing equipment without trained personnel or sustainable funding would not solve every problem. The missions therefore raised questions about the whole structure of government rather than supplying a simple technical shopping list.
